newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

A poll carried out by the Metropolitan Police Federation has found that the vast majority of London police constables are critical of the way the Met is being run. Criticisms include the inadequate number of police on the beat, ineffective use of resources, and Sir Paul Condon's new tenure career structure, which is to be introduced this summer.
-- RACAL PULLOUT BLOW TO TOP PFI SCHEME

Racal has withdrawn its bid for a major PFI scheme to build a secure radio communications system for police forces in England and Wales, on grounds that the risk involved was too high. This will come as a big blow to the Government, which had just said it wanted to revitalise ways of bringing private funding into public sector projects. Racal's decision to withdraw its bid now leaves the field clear for BT.
-- BROWN URGED TO SIMPLIFY TAX IN BUDGET

John Andrews, who today becomes the president of the 10,000 strong Chartered Institute of Taxation, has put forward radical proposals for the simplification of taxation which he hopes will be taken up by Chancellor Gordon Brown in his first Budget. The suggestions include the abolition of separate tax systems for salaried employees on Schedule E and those regarded as self- employed on Schedule D.
The dollar fell to a five-month low against the Japanese currency today, going beneath the 113 level and leading traders to believe it could drop much further.
